referencePatternsToCopy.label: Event detail and RSVP flow
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy an event detail layout: title, date/time, location, host, capacity/status chip, attendee context, RSVP action, and confirmation state.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Apple HIG navigation and content organization
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Make navigation predictable, content-centered, and appropriate for the userâ€™s current task.

findings.title: App Shell presentation states are not screenshot-proven
findings.summary: Existing screenshots show tabbed community screens, but they do not prove the required minimized, medium/in-focus, and expanded/maximized states or tap-to-expand transition for the same workflow/persona surface.
findings.visibleTextExcerpt: Spring Planting Workshop | Hands-on bed prep, seedling swap, and seasonal planning with Garden Club members. | Sat, Apr 18 | 10:00 AM | Riverside Greenhouse | 18 of 24 spots | Your RSVP | Choose Going, Maybe, or Not going after checking the schedule, location, host, and capacity. | RSVP to event | Care and volunteers | Private requests, volunteer shifts, and member support. | Basil seedlings offer | Offer six Sweet Genovese starter pots, choose pickup details, and control what contact info is shared. | Sweet Genovese basil | 6 starter pots | Pickup Sat 1-3 PM | Contact after claim | Members will see the plant variety, pickup window, privacy note, and how to claim the offer. | Offer plant | Garden Club | Home | Calendar | Documents | Marketplace
findings.requiredFix: Recapture and, if needed, implement the App Shell so Garden Club workflow surfaces visibly demonstrate minimized off-focus cards, a medium in-focus card, and a tap-expanded product surface for the same workflow/persona. The after screenshots must show the transition and the action surface, not just a static card list.

findings.title: Pinned surfaces are not proven in current screenshots
findings.summary: The product docs require persona-specific tabs and pinned surfaces, but the current screenshot evidence does not mark or prove which surface is pinned in each reviewed persona tab, nor that pinned content remains visible while other surfaces scroll.
findings.visibleTextExcerpt: Clubhouse Room A reservation | The homeowner record now shows owner, amount or decision, status history, and member next steps. | Event details | Property | Lot 42, homeowner Avery Brooks, Cedar Commons HOA; sender is the HOA board. | Record | Community Rules, Room A reservation, dues receipt, or architectural case. | History | Status, reviewer, receipt, version, timestamp, availability, and notification history remain visible. | Cedar Commons | Receipt/audit | Documents | HOA record saved | After you respond | The saved result keeps status, history, and change actions visible for this community task. | Owner inbox | Homeowner sees receipt, decision, document, reservation availability, sender, timestamp, and status. | Change option | Cancel reservation, request changes, retry payment, or reopen where policy allows. | Change RSVP | Add to calendar | Invite member | Saved | Cedar Commons HOA | Home | Giving | Board
findings.requiredFix: Update the community product doc or UI to identify pinned surfaces per persona/tab, then recapture screenshots proving pinned surfaces stay visible in the correct tab while non-pinned surfaces use minimized/medium/expanded behavior.

findings.title: Main community selection card presentation states are missing from evidence
findings.summary: B25 currently reviews community interior workflow screens, but it does not include screenshot-backed proof that the Loom Communities main selection page uses minimized/medium presentation states, scroll-driven focus, theme tokens, or tap-to-open behavior for community cards.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Is the UI modern, easy to use, easy to navigate, and visually appealing for target community personas?
holisticQuestionAnswers.why: The fresh screenshots show a cohesive mobile product shell with community-specific theming, persistent bottom tabs, readable cards/detail surfaces, and action areas that fit the target community context.

referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy a search layout with query, filters, ranked results, citations/sources, empty/error states, and follow-up actions.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Apple HIG navigation and content organization
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Make navigation predictable, content-centered, and appropriate for the userâ€™s current task.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Match schedule and result pattern
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy a match surface with players, schedule/round, result entry, result state, and next action.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Make navigation predictable, content-centered, and appropriate for the userâ€™s current task.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Inbox and message thread pattern
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy an inbox/thread structure: sender, timestamp, message preview/body, reply field, invite/block state, and read/received state.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Apple HIG navigation and content organization
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Make navigation predictable, content-centered, and appropriate for the userâ€™s current task.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Review-and-confirm payment flow
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use a review/confirmation step with amount, payer context, recipient, fees or entitlement, receipt, and audit trail.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Multi-step payment/progress flow
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use explicit progress states for checkout, review, confirmation, receipt, and entitlement/status.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Apple HIG navigation and content organization
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Make navigation predictable, content-centered, and appropriate for the userâ€™s current task.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material detail surface composition
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Build a domain detail page with primary content, metadata, status, and actions instead of a generic task card.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material detail surface composition
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Build a domain detail page with primary content, metadata, status, and actions instead of a generic task card.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Apple HIG navigation and content organization
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Make navigation predictable, content-centered, and appropriate for the userâ€™s current task.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material detail surface composition
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Build a domain detail page with primary content, metadata, status, and actions instead of a generic task card.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Make navigation predictable, content-centered, and appropriate for the userâ€™s current task.
